newsitem.title: CANADA: Protesting loggers block Greenpeace ship in Canada.
newsitem.headline: Protesting loggers block Greenpeace ship in Canada.

text.p: Angry Canadian loggers prevented a ship owned by the environmental group Greenpeace from sailing on Wednesday on an expedition to the Arctic.

The Greenpeace vessel MV Arctic Sunrise was due to leave Vancouver for a two-month trip to document the effects of climate change in Alaska and northern Canada. But a protest organised by lumber workers delayed the voyage.

Unionized forestry workers upset about Greenpeace's campaign against logging in the old-growth forests of British Columbia have been picketing the vessel since Saturday. The harbour pilot required to guide the vessel out to sea refused to cross the picket line on Wednesday and a flotilla of logs was moved into position around the ship, blocking its path.
"It doesn't look like we are going anywhere," Greenpeace official Jeanne Moffatt told reporters. It was unclear when the vessel might sail.
Dave Haggard, president of the IWA-Canada union that represents lumber workers, said his members were using attention-getting tactics similar to those employed by Greenpeace around the world.
"It's time for retribution," he said. "We are taking action against people who are trying to put our people out of work. Our intent is to keep the ship in harbour."
Greenpeace said it wanted to hold discussions with the union and protestors because it felt its goals were aligned with those of forestry workers.

Greenpeace researchers hoped to gather information on the Arctic expedition on what they said were the consequences of human-induced climate change inlcuding melting glaciers, a shrinking Arctic ice pack, thawing permafrost and the loss of forests.
